newsitem.title: USA: DC CFO says new Barry budget still will not fly.
newsitem.headline: DC CFO says new Barry budget still will not fly.

text.p: District of Columbia Mayor Marion Barry on Tuesday proposed a second $3.3 billion budget for the city in fiscal 1998, but the city's chief financial officer again said the plan will not fly.

The city's financial control board on March 3 rejected a February 1 balanced budget proposal by Barry, which would have saved $50 million in fiscal 1998 through restructuring of about $300 million in city debt.

The city's CFO Anthony Williams and five-member control board opposed the debt restructuring. On March 3, the control board also said that the overall plan does not fund public safety and schools adequately and gave Barry 15 days to overhaul the plan.
Williams said on Tuesday that Barry's latest plan is an improvement, but still falls short.
He said, for instance, that Barry's proposed $20 million reduction for the city's department of corrections and his proposed $446 million for public schools do not fund those programs adequately.

"If they don't think there's enough money for public safety - and I think there is - they have the responsibility to identify where the money is going to come from," Barry said of Williams and the control board.
